options: A working starter chart with Chart.yaml, values.yaml, a templates/ directory, and helper templates
A running Deployment directly on the currently connected cluster
A compiled container image ready to push to a registry
A Terraform module for provisioning the cluster itself
questions.explain: helm create scaffolds a chart's file layout on disk — Chart.yaml, values.yaml, templates/, _helpers.tpl — it does not touch a cluster.

questions.q: In Chart.yaml, what is the difference between `version` and `appVersion`?
options: version is required but appVersion is ignored by Helm entirely
appVersion sets the Kubernetes API version the chart targets
version is the chart's own version; appVersion is the version of the application the chart currently deploys, and the two move independently
They are two different ways of writing the exact same value and must always match
questions.explain: version tracks changes to the chart's templates/defaults; appVersion tracks the application image the chart points at by default — a chart can be patched without the app changing, or vice versa.

questions.q: What does `{{ include "myapp.fullname" . }}` do inside a template file?
options: Calls a named template defined in _helpers.tpl instead of repeating that logic in every manifest
Deletes the fullname field from the rendered manifest
Installs a dependency chart named myapp.fullname
Forces Helm to skip rendering that particular resource
questions.explain: _helpers.tpl defines reusable named templates; include calls one of them so naming/labeling logic is written once and reused, not duplicated across templates/deployment.yaml, service.yaml, and the rest.

options: Installs the chart onto whichever cluster kubectl is currently pointed at
Permanently deletes the chart's templates directory
Pushes the chart to a remote chart repository
Renders the chart to plain YAML locally, with no cluster interaction, so you can review the output before installing
questions.explain: helm template renders the final manifests exactly as helm install would generate them, without touching a cluster — useful for reviewing output before it goes anywhere real.

options: Network latency between the chart and the cluster's API server
Structural problems in the chart and missing required values, without installing anything
Whether the container image referenced by the chart has known vulnerabilities
Whether the chart has already been installed on the current cluster
questions.explain: helm lint validates a chart's structure and required values locally; it doesn't scan images or touch a cluster.
